## p104 A3 — Third-part radio acknowledgment instruction; near-copy reference 104359 preserved

**Edition context:** November 2: acknowledgment instructions and a conflicting copy.

**Related source pages:** [p105 C1](105.md#source-p105-c1), [p106 A2](106.md#source-p106-a2), [p106 A3](106.md#source-p106-a3).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-telegram-acknowledgments-november-2-acknowledgment-instructions-and-a-conflicting-copy"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The matching `FUER UKS 2/11 1300 3 TEILE` headers on pp105–106 identify three numbered parts. Their **636 native coordinates** give **318/318 fixed raw positions** without any repair. The page-local C/A section labels remain in the physical record identifiers.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-telegram-acknowledgments-p104-a3"></a>

### p104 A3

Childs p104, PDF p107; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p104_A3.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

**Meaning:** A surviving third part requests future radio acknowledgment of every telegram. Its reference is literally 104359, and its date conflicts with the near-copy elsewhere in this edition.

#### Earlier-page third-part witness

The p104 source says that parts 1 and 2 are missing and dates its message `1/11`; the three-part copy is dated `2/11`. The p104 body differs from p106 A3 in exactly **source coordinate 54**, V versus X. That changes **plaintext position 68** from 3 to 6: `104359` versus `104659`. Both sources are kept unchanged. The shared wording supports a near-copy relationship, not permission to overwrite either date or reference.

```text
FUR COS SS BERLIN W20 1240 SS BERLIN W43 1241 SS BERLIN W14 1350 VE 1537 (2/11)
RIZI-102
```

**Raw output — native 102-slot frame; 50/51 fixed positions:**

```text
VERBDGXMIT5UKSXGUTXRERMITTLGXNSMXNICHT?OETIGX6NKJXX
```

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **82 A→G**.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Verbdg. mit 5UKS gut. Vermittlg. NSM nicht noetig. 6NKJ.

**Meaning:** The link to 5UKS is reported good and mediation through NSM unnecessary. The 5, 6 and NSM remain literal output labels; they are not replaced by presumed spaces or OSM.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-uks-connection-interpretation-limits"></a>

### Interpretation limits

The damaged source slot belongs to the adjective `NOETIG`; the local fill does not solve a numerical key assignment. The exact output `5UKS`, `NSM` and `6NKJ` is preserved in every layer. In particular, the readily guessed station spelling OSM is not imposed on the received `NSM`. The report establishes only what the sender stated about the connection.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-uks-connection-attribution-and-reproducibility"></a>

## p104 C1, p104 C2 — Return to a replacement unit on medical grounds

<a id="edition-cases-people-medical-return-to-unit-return-to-a-replacement-unit-on-medical-grounds"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two p104 C parts report being sent to a replacement unit for specialist
medical treatment and recovery. The literal closing contains both
`RETTERL` and `KETTERL`, followed by `LTN`; neither spelling is silently
replaced by the other. The office-like field `DTSCHXSTAAT` remains unresolved.

Part 1 has a visibly short cipher group and remains conditional on one
missing transmitted coordinate. Part 2 has an ordinary complete frame.
Together the edition requires four known-coordinate substitutions and the
one separately charged insertion. No square label changes.

<a id="edition-cases-people-medical-return-to-unit-source-and-header"></a>

### Source and header

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, [printed p104, PDF p107](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [full page](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/sources/childs_p104_full.png)
places these parts under a November 2 heading. Their reception line says
November 4:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
C) POT v NKJ (9.10 a.m., November 4th)
FÜR POT FÜR HAFENKDTR 1135 (2) 2 TLE
1 TL RICHI-228
2 TL RICHI-140
```

</details>

The unchanged published `Nov1-3` key applies. The heading, internal day `(2)`
and later reception date are preserved without renaming the key period.

<a id="edition-cases-people-medical-return-to-unit-c1-one-coordinate-missing-from-the-source-frame"></a>

### C1: one coordinate missing from the source frame

The [first-part crop](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/sources/childs_p104_C1.png)
contains **227 valid coordinates**, although its label says 228. Group 34,
row 5/group 2, is visibly only **`GAGA`**, beginning at zero-based source
index 165. This is not merely an odd OCR extraction: the four-character
group is present in the image.

The unmodified 227-slot frame gives an unreadable 113-position string plus
an unpaired coordinate; that result is preserved in the certificate. Under
the conditional 228-slot model, inserting an unknown coordinate at index
168 gives 113 fixed labels out of 114:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional insertion at source index 168:**

```text
W?RDEHEUTEAUFGRUNDAERZTLXGUTACHTJDSEITENSSCHWARZMEERSTELLEDTSCHXSTAATZUSPEZIALAERZTLXBEHADDLUNGUXWIEDERHERSTELLUNG
```

</details>

Inserting `A` and applying three source-coordinate substitutions gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same conditional missing-slot frame, with A supplied and three substitutions:**

```text
WURDEHEUTEAUFGRUNDAERZTLXGUTACHTENSEITENSSCHWARZMEERSTELLEDTSCHXSTAATZUSPEZIALAERZTLXBEHANDLUNGUXWIEDERHERSTELLUNG
```

</details>

The phrase continues directly into part 2. It says that action was taken
today on the basis of a medical opinion from the `SCHWARZMEERSTELLE`
followed by the literal `DTSCHXSTAAT` field, for specialist medical treatment
and restoration of health. This edition does not turn `STAAT` into `STAB`
or assign a specific institutional identity.

<a id="edition-cases-people-medical-return-to-unit-equal-a-insertion-ambiguity"></a>

#### Equal-A insertion ambiguity

All **228** possible insertion positions were priced against the later
114-character template. The minimum is three observed-coordinate
substitutions, reached at positions **168, 169 and 170**, always with a
missing `A`. The three choices produce **one identical completed cipher
stream and one identical repaired received witness**.

Positions 168 and 169 lie within or at the end of the visibly short `GAGA`
group. Position 170 is just beyond it, after the first `A` of the next
printed group. It remains an arithmetic equivalent because the completed
stream contains three consecutive A coordinates there; it is not an
independently witnessed location of the source gap.

| Proposed insertion index | Where the unknown label appears before filling | Relationship to the short group |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 168 | `W?RDE` | Within `GAGA` |
| 169 | `A?FGRUND` | At the end of `GAGA` |
| 170 | `AE?ZTL` | Just beyond the printed short group |

The certificate preserves all three mappings from observed coordinates to
plaintext. The template was chosen after reading the message; this pricing
is not an independently supplied crib or proof of a uniquely placed loss.

<a id="edition-cases-people-medical-return-to-unit-c2-completion-of-the-sentence-and-the-literal-closing"></a>

### C2: completion of the sentence and the literal closing

The [second-part crop](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/sources/childs_p104_C2.png)
has exactly 140 valid coordinates and 70 fixed raw labels:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DERGESUNDHEITZUMERSATZTRUPPJNTEILINMARSHGESETZTXXRETTERLXKETTERLXLTNXX
```

</details>

One known-coordinate substitution gives:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DERGESUNDHEITZUMERSATZTRUPPENTEILINMARSHGESETZTXXRETTERLXKETTERLXLTNXX
```

</details>

Together the parts report being sent to the replacement unit for specialist
treatment and recovery. The source spells the phrase `IN MARSH GESETZT`;
no extra plaintext `C` is inserted to make modern `MARSCH`. Both name tokens
in `RETTERL KETTERL LTN` remain literal. The text supports a lieutenant's
medical-return report, not a unique historical identification from a repaired
surname.

<a id="edition-cases-people-medical-return-to-unit-costs-and-reproduction"></a>

### Costs and reproduction

All indices below refer to the **original received source**, before the
missing C1 coordinate is reconstructed. Printed group numbers and positions
are counted separately within each part.

| Part | Source index | Printed group / position | Change | Effect |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | 194 | 40 / 1 | `A` → `G` | `J` → `E` in `GUTACHTEN` |
| C1 | 200 | 41 / 2 | `A` → `G` | `BEHADDLUNG` → `BEHANDLUNG` |
| C1 | 218 | 44 / 5 | `A` → `G` | Final `D` → `N` in `GUTACHTEN` |
| C2 | 61 | 13 / 2 | `A` → `G` | `TRUPPJNTEIL` → `TRUPPENTEIL` |

The extra reconstructed `A` in C1 is charged as one **missing transmitted
coordinate**, not as a source-glyph fill. There are no unreadable coordinates
in either observed body. The [inputs](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/inputs.json)
and [certificates](../../experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/certificates.json)
preserve every original group, raw domain, insertion alternative, edit and
full/received forward witness.

```sh
python experiments/inventory_and_medical_return/verify.py --verify
```

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
also reproduced in Lasry's 2017 key comment. Earlier unreviewed OCR candidates
existed. No universal first-decipherment claim is made from the bounded
author-paper review. The conditional reconstruction certifies its arithmetic
and repair cost, while the source gap and unresolved words remain explicit.


<a id="edition-cases-people-meier-berlin-order"></a>

## p104 D — Batum lieutenant ordered to Berlin; one missing A restores the full order

**Edition context:** Batum: Lieutenant Meier ordered to Berlin.

<a id="edition-cases-people-meier-berlin-order-batum-lieutenant-meier-ordered-to-berlin"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The source advertises **RICHI-150** but contains **149 typed coordinates**. The fifth group in row 3 is visibly `ADAG`, containing four symbols. Supplying one **A** produces `ADAAG` and a complete **75-position** reading without changing any observed coordinate. The recovery is conditional on that local missing-coordinate model.

<a id="source-p104-d"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-meier-berlin-order-p104-d"></a>

### p104 D

Childs p104, PDF p107; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p104_D.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
D) POT v NKJ (8.36 a.m., November 4th)
POT ZUR UBERMITTLUNG NACH BATUM (2) 1650
RICHI-150
```

**Raw output — conditional 150-slot frame, inserting one unknown coordinate at source boundary 103; 74/75 fixed positions:**

```text
LTXMEIERXBATUMXSO?ORTBERLINABREISENXBEIMERSXBATLX2XGARDEREGTXMELDENXMILMISS
```

**Edited output — 0 observed-coordinate substitutions; 0 source-mask fills; 1 fill in the hypothesized added slot; same conditional frame; 75/75 fixed positions:**

```text
LTXMEIERXBATUMXSOFORTBERLINABREISENXBEIMERSXBATLX2XGARDEREGTXMELDENXMILMISS
```

</details>

The full edited stream re-encrypts exactly under the declared frame and listed changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Lt. Meier. Batum. Sofort Berlin abreisen. Beim Ers. Batl. 2. Garderegt. melden. Milmiss.

**Meaning:** The conditional reading orders Lieutenant Meier at Batum to leave immediately for Berlin and report to the replacement battalion designated 2. Garderegt. It does not prove that the journey occurred or establish a biographical identity.

<a id="edition-cases-people-meier-berlin-order-two-compatible-locations-for-the-same-missing-a"></a>

### Two compatible locations for the same missing A

All five insertion boundaries within the short group are checked against the complete proposed text:

| Source boundary | Added value | Observed-coordinate substitutions |
|---|---|---:|
| 100 | A | 2 |
| 101 | D | 1 |
| 102 | A | 0 |
| 103 | A | 0 |
| 104 | G | 1 |

The two zero-substitution alignments produce **the same complete ciphertext and the same plaintext**. Their raw uncertainty differs: boundary 102 leaves the last letter of `MEIER` unresolved; boundary 103 leaves a letter of `SOFORT` unresolved. Neither alignment is preferred as the exact historical loss location. The displayed raw stream uses boundary 103, with the alternative retained in the certificate. The finite comparison concerns this local short-group model and proposed wording, not every imaginable corruption mechanism.

The unit number 2 remains the published-square label, and `ERS`, `BATL`, `GARDEREGT` and `MILMISS` are not silently expanded in the complete German display. No specific biography of Meier is asserted.

## p104 E3 — Reserve Jaeger battalion commander consents to transfer; unit field unknown

**Edition context:** Sevastopol: consent to a personnel transfer.

<a id="edition-cases-people-sevastopol-transfer-consent-sevastopol-consent-to-a-personnel-transfer"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

<a id="source-p104-e3"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-sevastopol-transfer-consent-p104-e3"></a>

### p104 E3

Childs p104, PDF p107; [reviewed source crop](../../experiments/nov2_acknowledgments_and_personnel/sources/p104_E3.png). Key: unchanged published **Nov1–3**.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Source transcription — literal received header:**

```text
E) POT v NKJ (9.06 a.m., November 4th)
0810 (2)
3 TL RICHI-140
```

**Raw output — native 140-slot frame; 68/70 fixed positions:**

```text
KOMDEURXRESXJ?EGXBATLX?ISTMITVERSETZGXEINRERSTANDEDXXGOUVXSEWASTOPOLXX
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions; 1 source-mask fill; 69/70 fixed positions:**

```text
KOMDEURXRESXJAEGXBATLX?ISTMITVERSETZGXEINVERSTANDENXXGOUVXSEWASTOPOLXX
```

</details>

Observed source changes, with zero-based indices: **41 A→G**, **130 A→G**.

Source-mask fills: **119 C→G**.

The coordinate-pair certificate verifies every fixed candidate position and retains the unresolved source mask. A complete plaintext re-encryption is not claimed for the remaining unknown position.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Komdeur. Res. Jaeg. Batl. ? ist mit Versetzg. einverstanden. Gouv. Sewastopol.

**Meaning:** A surviving third part says that the commander of a reserve Jaeger battalion agrees to a transfer. The battalion field remains unknown. The signature gives the Sevastopol governor abbreviation; no officer identity is supplied.

<a id="edition-cases-people-sevastopol-transfer-consent-unresolved-unit-and-source-glyphs"></a>

### Unresolved unit and source glyphs

The source prints C-like noncoordinate glyphs in `GAAXC` and `GXAVC`, at source indices **39** and **119**. The latter is supplied as G to read `JAEG`; the former remains masked. Its resulting one-position battalion field is the literal `?` in both the edited stream and readable display. There is no assignment of an assumed battalion number.

The two observed-coordinate changes repair `EINRERSTANDED` to `EINVERSTANDEN`. The remaining abbreviations, including `KOMDEUR`, remain as transmitted. This source is explicitly part 3; the absent first two parts are not reconstructed.
